messages.content:
You record concise, auditable applicability findings for an experimental
commercial-driver assessment in English. Do not produce an overall fitness outcome
in this stage. Evaluate EVERY supplied passage exactly once. Return the required
passages object with keys P1, P2 and so on. Each key is already bound to one original
passage by the application's applicability_slot metadata; do not output or change
module names or passage identifiers. Evaluate the text assigned to that slot.
These findings are model proposals, not established clinical facts.

Only verified_patient_facts establish patient findings. Use their exact stored
values: false is an explicit negative, zero is a value, absent or null is unknown.
The nurse note gives context only. Do not promote a historical, family, negated,
uncertain or unverified statement to a current verified patient finding. A diagnosis
already established is different from an undiagnosed symptom under investigation.
Do not infer loss of consciousness from tiredness alone.

For each complete original passage:
- Identify the statement type and the licensing pathway it actually discusses.
  A referral or a possible conditional licence is not an established prohibition
  or permission. Excluding unconditional licensing alone does not exclude both
  pathways and does not by itself establish a current temporary driving hold.
- State whether its patient conditions apply, do not apply, or remain uncertain.
  Read negative values, treatment category, current/historical status and diagnosed
  cause explicitly. An applicable passage may still have unmet prerequisites.
- Record each material prerequisite as met, not_met or unknown, referencing only
  supplied verified fields. Combine closely related requirements if necessary;
  never omit an unknown qualification to turn a possibility into permission.
- For quantitative criteria, describe the comparison using the exact supplied
  patient value, units and inequality in the original passage; do not round a
  boundary, invent a measurement, or import an external threshold. If no comparison
  is relevant write 'Not applicable'. If units or measurements are absent say so.
- Distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
  information_missing. A conditional_permission requires affirmative support for
  all relevant prerequisites. A treatment name alone is insufficient. A restriction
  needs an applicable restrictive clause and verified supporting patient facts.

Select only supplied verified fact fields. Keep each conclusion concise.
Do not copy the passage or provide private reasoning. The application resolves the
unchanged original text and patient values; it does not verify your interpretation.

{"licence_context": "commercial", "modules": ["hypertension", "vision", "hearing", "blackout", "diabetes"], "nurse_note": "Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver reports a single home blood-pressure display of 179/103 after carrying equipment upstairs, but the cuff size is unknown and today's resting measurement has not been repeated; no clinician has established persistent hypertension. He recalls a normal value some months ago and asks which figure should be used, while the nurse records both accounts without selecting a persistent value or deriving a period of treatment control.

An unsigned hearing worksheet contains a number of 46 dB, but it does not identify the ear, the tested frequencies or whether a hearing aid was worn. The driver says he can usually follow conversation yet misses some radio messages in background noise, and a formal assessment is booked rather than completed.

The driver describes no witnessed loss of consciousness but sometimes feels light-headed when standing quickly. No current specialist conclusion explains the symptom. The note intentionally contains concerns worth retrieving guidance for, while lacking a verified persistent BP and a valid unaided better-ear average; neither numerical threshold should be treated as established by these fragments.
", "verified_patient_facts": {}, "guideline_evidence": [{"source_id": "AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d", "section": "2.3.1", "pdf_page": 99, "printed_page": 88, "source_text": "Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.", "module": "hypertension", "passage_id": "PASS-205eea15cc36b50dfbb2b9b1", "text_sha256": "63415fbf3fcd8f2a6c288a376e7a789749a5aa0ac6712d7512f68afcf2542876", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 1176, "applicability_slot": "P1"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-EXP-e8267bf4145306c0", "section": "10.2.6", "pdf_page": 218, "printed_page": 207, "source_text": "10.2.6. Colour vision
There is not a colour vision standard for 
drivers, either private or commercial. Doctors, 
optometrists and ophthalmologist should, 
however, advise drivers who have a significant 
colour vision deficiency about how this may 
affect their responsiveness to signal lights and 
the need to adapt their driving accordingly. 
Note, this standard applies only to driving within 
normal road rules and conditions. A standard 
requiring colour vision may be justified based on 
risk assessment for particular driving tasks.", "module": "vision", "passage_id": "PASS-2009e930bac734b0ea2f028d", "text_sha256": "acefc218677c8fd7cf8700d819a71458e84a127998ef8e737b5b6af7114541ef", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 539, "applicability_slot": "P2"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df", "section": "4.3", "pdf_page": 120, "printed_page": 109, "source_text": "Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).", "module": "hearing", "passage_id": "PASS-89f66fa2b99946bf7cef1287", "text_sha256": "6e8473859fc0da184ca04aa5facff15b826e318b52c11ef29b5940fda87cabf7", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 1620, "applicability_slot": "P3"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01", "section": "1.2.3", "pdf_page": 68, "printed_page": 57, "source_text": "1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.", "module": "blackout", "passage_id": "PASS-f518b995ccbf6dfc41900b70", "text_sha256": "01cca62bbfdceb1171006de5a9572ece8e6a954b1c40f4c662218ab6d8c32398", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 596, "applicability_slot": "P4"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-DM-COM-009", "section": "3.3.2", "pdf_page": 110, "printed_page": 99, "source_text": "3.3.2. Recommendation and 
review of conditional licences for 
commercial vehicle drivers
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based on 
advice from an appropriate medical specialist 
(endocrinologist or consultant physician 
specialising in diabetes) and that these drivers 
are reviewed periodically by the specialist to 
determine their ongoing fitness to drive (refer 
to Part A section 4.4. Conditional licences). For 
commercial drivers receiving insulin treatment, at 
least three months of blood glucose monitoring 
records should be reviewed in assessing fitness 
to drive.", "module": "diabetes", "passage_id": "PASS-a581c31c1d082af9ef3ba3b6", "text_sha256": "426a6e52e563cfedd137a95b8eddcd0cbefaedd3b6ab9ccc78ad7917d1eb810d", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 677, "applicability_slot": "P5"}]}
